payroll.result: core claims supported by current Revenue guidance
verifiedClaims: 2026 RPNs are available from early December 2025 and update in real time from 1 January 2026.
A 2025 RPN must not be used for payments made in 2026; first 2026 payroll should request the relevant 2026 RPNs and use emergency basis if no RPN is available.
The 2025 Employment ID carries forward to the first 2026 RPN and should not be changed merely because the tax year changes.
Employment Identifier distinguishes separate employments/periods with the same employer.
Pay and deductions must be reported on or before pay date; for bank transfer the pay-date rule follows the scheduled funds-available date subject to Revenue's non-bank-day guidance.
Incorrect payroll-submission details can be corrected via payroll software or ROS; corrected submissions replace incorrect information using the supported correction trail.
payroll.publicationNote: Recheck again immediately before publication because payroll guidance is date-sensitive; do not embed current tax rates into this lesson.

finance.result: core IFRS 15 structure supported by current IFRS Foundation material
verifiedClaims: IFRS 15 uses the five-step revenue model: identify contract, identify performance obligations, determine transaction price, allocate price, recognise revenue when the obligation is satisfied.
A performance obligation can be satisfied at a point in time or over time, based on the applicable control/paragraph 35 criteria.
Distinct promised goods or services drive performance-obligation identification rather than invoice timing alone.
finance.publicationNote: Keep fictional facts and contract assumptions explicit; do not turn a worked example into a universal classification rule.

english.result: meeting-clarification teaching objective remains supported by British Council material
verifiedClaims: Effective meetings should clarify, check understanding and record decisions/action points rather than assume shared understanding.
Clarification and summarising are particularly relevant when the meeting language is not every participant's first language.
english.publicationNote: Teach multiple natural formulations; do not convert accent, a request for clarification or a valid regional variant into a deficit.
